facts.fact: Leaves Kairon to study on Ananke, the administrative world at the center of the governing system
facts.quote: a young woman named Nora Hale leaves the capital planet Kairon to study on Ananke — the administrative world where the system that governs human continuity is centered

facts.fact: Loves Iris; the love does not stop even after learning the truth about her
facts.quote: because returning was what you did when you loved someone, and she loved Iris, and the loving had not stopped, and the not-stopping was the thing that made the knowledge bearable and unbearable

facts.fact: Defines herself by never stopping asking questions
facts.quote: I don't stop asking questions.

facts.fact: Habitually watches the crowd rather than the speaker at public events, an old observational habit
facts.quote: Nora was watching the crowd rather than the speaker — an old habit, learned across years of observation that the most useful information in any public forum was rarely on the official platform.

facts.fact: Takes no written notes; retains what matters through memory of body language and syntax
facts.quote: Nora took no notes. Her notes lived in the specific quality of what had been said and what had been declined, in the crowd's body language and the speakers' syntax

facts.fact: Repeatedly holds Iris's dangerously overheated hands, overriding her own withdrawal reflex
facts.quote: Nora held her burning hands. She held them the way she had held them in the café on Ananke, the way she had held them in the cabin of the transit vessel

facts.fact: Writes journalism with restraint, letting the arrangement of facts do the work instead of commentary
facts.quote: the journalism residing in the selection and arrangement of facts rather than in commentary about them

facts.fact: After the bombing her face changes not in its features but in its set (jaw angle, weight behind the eyes)
facts.quote: the woman whose face had changed not in its features but in its set, the jaw differently angled, the eyes carrying a depth that was not wisdom but weight

facts.fact: Shorter than Iris by several centimeters
facts.quote: She was tall — taller than Nora by several centimeters

facts.fact: Twenty-two years old at the story's start
facts.quote: the accumulated sediment of twenty-two years of living in a place

facts.fact: Her mother managed a community resource exchange and taught her that showing up daily was the most political act a person could perform
facts.quote: her mother, who managed a community resource exchange, had taught her by example that the most political act a person could perform was the daily act of showing up to help

facts.fact: Her father left the family when she was eleven, having loved the idea of elsewhere slightly more than staying
facts.quote: her father, who had left when she was eleven — not dramatically, not badly, but with the quiet departure of a person who had loved his family but had loved the idea of elsewhere slightly more

facts.fact: Studied under Professor Mareth on Kairon before going to Ananke, a course that reshaped how she understood the place
facts.quote: Then in Mareth's course, where it becomes something else, something with edges and implications and all the parts the photographs don't show

facts.fact: In later years spent twenty years in political journalism and speaks or recognizes eight languages
facts.quote: any of the eight languages Nora spoke or recognized or had encountered in twenty years of political journalism across the settled systems

facts.fact: Breaks the story on the leaked memo phrase 'acceptable operational degradation'
facts.quote: She wrote about the phrase "acceptable operational degradation" and its institutional lineage

facts.fact: Lives the double role of Iris's loving partner and, secretly, her investigator
facts.quote: the partner who loved Iris and the investigator who watched her, the tenderness and the scrutiny occupying the same hours, the same gestures, the same shared meals and conversations

facts.fact: Close, long friendship with Esen from Kairon, communicated in a private shorthand of their own
facts.quote: not words but the shape of feeling, rendered in the alphabet of a friendship that had developed its own syntax

antiFacts.claim: Nora has red or blonde hair
antiFacts.why: Her hair color is never stated anywhere in the text; only Iris's and Helia's physical traits are described in that kind of detail.

antiFacts.claim: Nora wears glasses
antiFacts.why: No mention of eyewear for Nora exists; the only 'glasses' hits in the text are drinking glasses in unrelated scenes.

antiFacts.claim: Nora carries or uses a weapon
antiFacts.why: She is a journalist and observer throughout; the text never depicts her arming herself or using a weapon.

antiFacts.claim: Nora and Iris get married
antiFacts.why: No wedding or marriage proposal between Nora and Iris appears in the text; their bond is expressed through cohabitation and shared routine, not a marriage plot.

antiFacts.claim: Nora has siblings
antiFacts.why: The text discusses her mother and father individually but never mentions a sibling.

facts.fact: Tall, taller than Nora by several centimeters
facts.quote: She was tall — taller than Nora by several centimeters

facts.fact: Skin/hands notably warmer than ambient temperature
facts.quote: Iris's hand was warm. Notably warm — warmer than the ambient temperature should have produced, warmer than Nora's own hand

facts.fact: Dark, warm, mobile eyes
facts.quote: Iris's eyes were dark and warm and mobile, full of the specific intelligence that comes from curiosity

facts.fact: Has a scar on the inner left forearm near the wrist from a cooking burn
facts.quote: I have a scar," Iris said. She touched her left forearm — the inner surface, near the wrist.

facts.fact: Shares the exact same facial bone structure and geometry as Helia, in a different register
facts.quote: The face Nora was looking at was Iris's face, transposed into a different register: where Iris's features were warm, this face was cool

facts.fact: Constantly touches surfaces to orient herself; says touch tells her where she is
facts.quote: I like knowing where I am," Iris said. "Touch tells me where I am.

facts.fact: Her warmth is genuine, not performed, and seems to alter the space around her
facts.quote: The smile was warm. Not performed-warm — actually warm, the kind of warmth that enters a space and rearranges it

facts.fact: Prefers old, worn, imperfect things over engineered perfection
facts.quote: Because it's true. Perfection is a performance.

facts.fact: Has a full, unexpectedly loud laugh that disrupts Ananke's calibrated acoustic environment
facts.quote: The laugh that came from Iris was full and unexpected and had a quality that did not match the controlled acoustic environment of the campus

facts.fact: Identifies herself as a long-time "resident" of Ananke, not a student, professor, or administrator
facts.quote: Iris was not a student, not a professor, not an administrator. She was — and the word she used was "resident,"

facts.fact: Has never experienced real rain, only controlled precipitation events
facts.quote: I've never been in rain.

facts.fact: Implies she existed in some other form before settling into this body
facts.quote: the body was strange. Not wrong. Not uncomfortable. Just — unfamiliar. Like wearing clothing that fits perfectly but belongs to someone else.

facts.fact: Habitually presses her palms flat against surfaces, fingers spread, as if reading them
facts.quote: Iris's hands were always in contact with surfaces. She pressed her palm flat against the bench as they talked

facts.fact: Opens a locked rooftop door with a silent gesture rather than a key
facts.quote: the door at the top of the stairwell had a lock that Iris opened with a gesture Nora did not quite see, the lock responding to something that was not a key

facts.fact: Speaks in short, direct, aphoristic declarative statements
facts.quote: This is what happens when a surface stops performing and starts existing.

facts.fact: When bound by institutional constraint, conveys truth through embodiment philosophy and analogy rather than direct disclosure
facts.quote: The medium shapes the message. The vessel shapes the contents.

facts.fact: Initiates the relationship with Nora, approaching her unprompted at a campus dispensary and already having noticed her before formal introduction
facts.quote: I pay attention to who arrives. It's a habit.

facts.fact: Becomes Nora's romantic partner; later they share an apartment on Kairon
facts.quote: since they began sharing the apartment

facts.fact: When Nora confronts her with "I know what you are," her first reaction is relief, not fear
facts.quote: The first thing that crossed Iris's face was relief.

facts.fact: Repeatedly wants to tell Nora the full truth but says she is bound not to yet
facts.quote: I want to tell you everything," Iris said. "I need you to know that.

antiFacts.claim: Iris has blonde hair
antiFacts.why: The text never specifies Iris's hair color at all.

antiFacts.claim: Iris works as a professor or administrator at the Ananke academy
antiFacts.why: The text explicitly states she is not a student, not a professor, not an administrator, and calls herself a 'resident.'

antiFacts.claim: Iris and Nora are formally introduced by a mutual friend or through Mareth's class
antiFacts.why: Iris approaches Nora unprompted at a drink dispensary; there is no third-party introduction.

antiFacts.claim: Iris explicitly says the words 'I am Helia' or otherwise directly states in dialogue that she and Helia are the same entity
antiFacts.why: The connection is shown only through shared facial geometry, euphemism ('vessel', 'the fragment'), and implication; the manuscript never has her state it in those literal words.

antiFacts.claim: Iris has children
antiFacts.why: No children are ever mentioned for Iris in the text.

facts.fact: hollow, feature-less concave face with a single point of light instead of eyes/nose/mouth
facts.quote: It was hollow in the architectural sense: a shaped absence, a surface curving inward like the inside of a shallow bowl

facts.fact: white hair worn in a structured bob
facts.quote: A strand of white hair had come loose from the structured bob that framed her face

facts.fact: pale, long-fingered hands with pronounced knuckles
facts.quote: pale, long-fingered, the knuckles slightly too pronounced in a way that suggested the body had been optimized for precision rather than symmetry

facts.fact: runs hot in every body she wears
facts.quote: She ran hot — all her bodies did — and the heat had to go somewhere.

facts.fact: her original body (Body-A) has grey hair and lines around the eyes and had appeared on governance broadcasts for three decades
facts.quote: at this body, Body-A, the original, the one with the stone in its pocket and the lines around its eyes and the grey hair and the face that had been on governance broadcasts for three decades

facts.fact: has been "the Vessel" (the distributed consciousness administering the lattice/human continuity system) for thirty-eight years, inhabiting forty-seven bodies across eleven worlds and three orbital stations
facts.quote: Helia had been the Vessel for thirty-eight years. She inhabited, at this point in the record, forty-seven bodies distributed across eleven worlds and three orbital stations.

facts.fact: administers "the Vault", the archival chamber/infrastructure at the center of the governance system, on a data moon orbiting Ananke
facts.quote: the Vault needed to know who was walking through it in order to calibrate the archival medium's response. She was the only person whose footsteps the floor recognized without delay.

facts.fact: a fatigue-driven rounding error in an overloaded, feverish body caused the Crownfall atmospheric-processor cascade
facts.quote: Body-23 was running a fever. Not dangerous — 38.2 degrees Celsius, a low-grade elevation that the monitoring team would note and treat and that would resolve within a day.

facts.fact: authorized the Axiom Spire to fire on Crownfall's southern hemisphere, killing eleven thousand people to prevent an estimated three hundred thousand to four hundred seventy thousand deaths from the cascade ("the Necessary Fire")
facts.quote: Option two: the Axiom Spire — a capital ship at Crownfall's orbital junction whose directed energy system could cauterize the failing zone, destroying processors and settlements alike

facts.fact: recruited Orenna Vey into the integration process decades earlier; Orenna underwent "cognitive dissolution" and did not survive it, while Helia had survived the same process
facts.quote: Orenna was sitting in the chair where Helia had sat thirty-eight years ago. The symmetry was not lost on either of them.

facts.fact: a year after the lattice ended, lives for the first time as a single embodied person, having not been "a person in rooms" in thirty years
facts.quote: She had not been a person in rooms in this sense for thirty years. She had been the room's governance architecture.

facts.fact: treats composure as a constant, effortful performance rather than a natural state, even alone
facts.quote: Composure, she had learned across a century of wearing it, was always a performance, even when the audience was yourself.

facts.fact: experiences mass casualties as both cold statistical correction and personal catastrophe at once, and refuses to excuse her own error
facts.quote: She felt the eleven thousand absences as a computational correction and as a catastrophe simultaneously, the dual registration the defining characteristic of her existence

facts.fact: refused to mitigate or explain away the Crownfall error, insisting on unqualified acknowledgment that she had made a mistake and people had died
facts.quote: She did not explain because the explanation, however accurate, would sound like mitigation, and the eleven thousand dead did not require mitigation.

facts.fact: smiling and easy laughter are rare for her; her ordinary laughter as the Vessel is functional and diplomatic rather than genuine
facts.quote: Helia smiled. The smile was genuine and that was rare. "I am tired."

facts.fact: has a recurring, unexplained habit of pressing her palm flat against surfaces to leave warmth in them
facts.quote: When she pressed her palm flat against surfaces, the material accepted the warmth of her hand the way water accepts a stone

facts.fact: commands fleet operations by floating, untethered, at the center of the Axiom Spire's zero-gravity "command core" to interface with the lattice
facts.quote: The body floated. The floating was the core's zero-gravity environment's physical fact — the fact of the gravitational absence allowing the body's mass to remain in the position

facts.fact: refers to her governing role in the detached third person as "the governance function" rather than "I", especially under pressure
facts.quote: "The governance function cannot hold the individual experience," Helia said.

facts.fact: speaks in terse, clipped, repetitive-clause institutional sentences broken by dashes
facts.quote: "The timeline is the timeline," Helia said. "If you need it explained twice, you are in the wrong room."

facts.fact: shares Iris Valen's exact bone structure and facial geometry, cool where Iris is warm
facts.quote: The geometry was the same. Not similar — the same. The face Nora was looking at was Iris's face, transposed into a different register

facts.fact: Iris Valen is lattice-connected to her as a fragment, feeling and partially perceiving through Helia during Helia's full operational engagements
facts.quote: The Meridian formation is — twelve vessels. She can see them. I can — I can almost see them. Through her.

facts.fact: during the Convergence explosion, her body seized on the same side that Iris's body collapsed at the same moment
facts.quote: The jerk was involuntary, a spasm that traveled through Helia's body from the right shoulder downward, the same side on which Iris had collapsed

facts.fact: was directly interviewed/confronted by journalist Nora Hale about the Crownfall dead, including the named victim Talis Moren
facts.quote: But Talis Moren is in the public record.

antiFacts.claim: Helia has blue or brown eyes
antiFacts.why: Her face is described as a hollow, feature-less concave surface with a single point of light standing in for an eye, not colored human eyes; even Body-A's eyes are never given a color.

antiFacts.claim: Helia laughs easily and often
antiFacts.why: The text states the opposite: her laughter is functional and diplomatic, and a genuine smile from her is called rare.

antiFacts.claim: Helia has living parents or a stated family of origin
antiFacts.why: No mother, father, or parents are ever mentioned for Helia in the text.

antiFacts.claim: Helia was born or raised on Kairon
antiFacts.why: No birthplace is ever stated; she is associated with Ananke, the Vault, and the lattice, never with an origin world.

antiFacts.claim: Helia always operates through a single body
antiFacts.why: For most of the novel she is explicitly distributed across dozens of simultaneous bodies (forty-seven at one count); living as literally "one body" is a late, temporary post-war state, not her default.

facts.fact: Commanded HEDA's defensive fleet for fourteen years before the war, a career defined by readiness without ever seeing deployment
facts.quote: Kael had commanded HEDA's defensive fleet for over a decade — a career defined by preparedness without deployment, now facing the arrival.

facts.fact: Doctrine is proportionality and restraint in the use of force
facts.quote: Kael's doctrine is proportionality.

facts.fact: Reputation for calibrated, non-wasteful use of military force
facts.quote: That's Kael. She doesn't waste ordnance and she doesn't waste credibility.

facts.fact: Ultimately subordinate to civilian/governance political authority despite commanding the fleet
facts.quote: Kael follows orders. The question is not what Kael will do. The question is what she will be told to do.

facts.fact: Chose to publish the mobilization order openly rather than classify it, a politically savvy move
facts.quote: Kael had chosen to publish. The choice was the first evidence that the Fleet Marshal understood the political landscape as well as the operational one.

facts.fact: Served under Helia's authority for fourteen peacetime years before the war
facts.quote: The Fleet Marshal had served under Helia's authority for fourteen years — the years that had been the peacetime years

facts.fact: Speaks in terse, economical reports; announced the Tessarine engagement's end with just "Fleet secured."
facts.quote: Kael observed the withdrawal from the platform. "Fleet secured." The statement was the simplest statement carrying the most weight

facts.fact: Drew rules of engagement that authorized only defensive fire and pursuit within the Drift Belt corridor, not offensive expansion of the war
facts.quote: The rules authorized defensive fire. The rules authorized pursuit within the Drift Belt corridor's operational boundaries. The rules did not authorize offensive operations beyond the corridor.

facts.fact: Answers questions from Helia/the governance function with single clipped words like "Understood"
facts.quote: "Understood," Kael said. The word was the military voice at its most economical

facts.fact: Accepts operational constraints rather than pushing to have them removed
facts.quote: Kael was the kind of commander who accepted constraints rather than demanding their elimination.

facts.fact: Addresses Helia formally as "Administrator" even after fourteen years of working relationship
facts.quote: "Administrator." Kael used the institutional address.

facts.fact: After the Tessarine engagement, personally carried water to Helia at the railing and stood quietly beside her rather than joining the debrief, without being asked
facts.quote: He had not asked if she wanted water. He had not said anything about what she had done. He had set the container on the ledge and stepped back to the position adjacent to her

facts.fact: Understood that Helia's power as a weapon was not unlimited but constrained by a finite biological/consciousness capacity, not just engineering
facts.quote: The understanding was the Fleet Marshal's most important capability: the capability of understanding that the weapon's power was not unlimited and that the limitation was not engineering but biological

facts.fact: Before being named, first appears as an unnamed watchful figure stationed at corridor junctions to maximize visual coverage, with a posture read as protective vigilance rather than active threat
facts.quote: the specific posture of a person whose professional mandate was the safety of the people around him and whose expression of that mandate was not active protection but passive awareness

antiFacts.claim: Kael has a described physical appearance (hair color, eye color, height, or face)
antiFacts.why: No passage in the manuscript describes Kael's face, hair, eyes, or build; all characterization is through action, doctrine, and terse dialogue.

antiFacts.claim: Kael has a spouse, children, or other family mentioned in the text
antiFacts.why: No family members, romantic partners, or childhood background are mentioned anywhere in Kael's appearances.

antiFacts.claim: Kael and Nora have a personal, informal relationship or ever meet face to face for an in-person interview
antiFacts.why: Nora's requested interview is only ever a scheduled press session under protocol; the text never depicts them meeting in person or developing rapport.

antiFacts.claim: Kael opposed or voted against the DAF (Informed Continuity Act / governance reform)
antiFacts.why: The text explicitly states Kael abstained rather than opposed, framed as deliberate neutrality, not opposition.

antiFacts.claim: Kael dies or is killed during the war
antiFacts.why: Kael's last confirmed appearance (the railing scene after the Tessarine engagement) is alive and functioning; no death is ever narrated.

facts.fact: Political philosophy professor at Nora's academy on Ananke, has taught there for 22 years
facts.quote: I have been teaching here for twenty-two years. The expression has not changed.

facts.fact: Academic reputation is quiet and peripheral: cited in footnotes by other scholars, never central to debate
facts.quote: always in footnotes, always referenced by other scholars, never at the center of debate but always at its edges

facts.fact: Warmth is a permanent, fundamental feature of his character, paired with an underlying tiredness
facts.quote: The warmth did not leave — the warmth was permanent, a feature of his character as fundamental as the tiredness.

facts.fact: Careful and guarded about what he says because of his decades of proximity to institutional power
facts.quote: Mareth was careful because he knew, with the certainty of decades of proximity to institutional power, exactly which observations were unwelcome and exactly what the consequences of making them could be.

facts.fact: Teaches with patient intensity, having repeated the same core ideas for decades yet still finding them evolve
facts.quote: Mareth taught with the patient intensity of a man who had been saying the same things for decades

facts.fact: Speaks in careful institutional metaphors, framing questions of who a system serves and what it costs
facts.quote: The question isn't whether the system works. The question is who it works for, and what it costs the people closest to its machinery.

facts.fact: Gives Nora handwritten, precise directions to a restricted Helios Institute archive room, including its door code
facts.quote: East wing, past the restoration lab, second door after the fire suppression panel, code 7-7-4-1, ask for nothing and touch only what's on the open shelves.

facts.fact: Iris calls him a good man in a careful position who tells Nora the truth but not the whole truth
facts.quote: Mareth is a good man in a careful position. What he told you is true.

facts.fact: Has tired, warm eyes that Nora associates with a certain kind of institutional knowledge
facts.quote: He looked at her with the tired, warm eyes that she had come to associate with a specific kind of institutional knowledge

facts.fact: His office is a small, disordered room in the lecture complex, cluttered with actual paper books
facts.quote: Books — actual books, paper and binding, more books than Nora had seen in any single room on Ananke — were stacked on every surface

facts.fact: Habitually drinks from a cup of tea or coffee that has gone cold without noticing or caring
facts.quote: He drank from the cold cup without noticing or caring that its contents were cold.

facts.fact: Advises Nora on practical travel details, recommending a longer, more comfortable transit route for reading
facts.quote: Take the Eddington Line, it stops at three stations but the seats are wider and you'll need the reading time

facts.fact: Has spent his whole career inside the institution, teaching its history and ethics while privately understanding more about its operations than his lectures reveal
facts.quote: a man who had spent his career inside the institution, teaching its history and its ethics while knowing, she now suspected, more about its operations than his lectures revealed

facts.fact: First pointed Nora toward the Helios Institute's records on the historical "Vessel program" that becomes central to her investigation
facts.quote: the history of the Vessel program that Mareth had pointed her toward

facts.fact: Treats noticing itself as a virtue rather than a problem, according to Iris
facts.quote: He's one of the few people here who still treats noticing as a virtue rather than a problem.

facts.fact: Regarded by Iris as one of the few people capable of forming an outside perspective on Ananke's system, unlike Iris herself
facts.quote: I can't step outside to form a perspective the way you can, the way Ilyon can, the way Mareth can.

facts.fact: When pressed on a sensitive question, deliberately stops himself at the edge of what he is willing to say rather than crossing it
facts.quote: He shook his head — not a refusal but a boundary, the gesture of a person who has reached the edge of what he can say in a room that might be listened to

antiFacts.claim: Mareth is described as elderly, with grey hair or a specific physical build/age given in the text
antiFacts.why: The text never gives his hair color, age in years, or physical build; only his eyes ('tired, warm') and general demeanor are described, despite 22 years of teaching being stated.

antiFacts.claim: Mareth is arrested, harmed, or killed as a consequence of Nora's investigation
antiFacts.why: No text states any such fate; his appearances show him simply continuing to guide Nora with no indication of retaliation against him.

antiFacts.claim: Mareth is originally from Kairon, the same homeworld as Nora
antiFacts.why: The text states Nora 'was the only one from Kairon' in his seminar, implying Mareth is not from Kairon; no origin planet is ever given for him.

antiFacts.claim: Mareth has a wife, husband, or is otherwise described as married
antiFacts.why: No mention of a spouse or romantic partner appears anywhere in his scenes; his personal life outside teaching and the archive is not depicted.

antiFacts.claim: Mareth personally travels to the frontier or takes part in the later war/military chapters of the book
antiFacts.why: His appearances are concentrated in the early academic-arc chapters, with a single retrospective mention much later; he is never shown in the later war/governance-crisis arcs.

facts.fact: compact frame, close-cropped grey hair, hands that move kinetically while she talks
facts.quote: Qesh stood. She was smaller than her reputation suggested. Compact frame, close-cropped grey hair, hands that moved when she talked in a way that was not theatrical but kinetic

facts.fact: has served as envoy for twelve years
facts.quote: She had been an envoy for twelve years.

facts.fact: reputation for precision and a controlled, cutting anger rather than shouting
facts.quote: She had a reputation for precision and for the kind of anger that did not shout but cut.

facts.fact: cross-examines HEDA witnesses at post-bombing hearings, adjusting tone to each subject (sharp with Tane, gentler with Hollis)
facts.quote: With Tane she had been sharp, adversarial, the questions designed to expose the gap between institutional language and human reality. With Hollis she was gentler, almost collegial

facts.fact: speaks without preamble or rhetorical framing, going straight to the mechanism of an issue
facts.quote: She did not preamble. She did not contextualize. She began with the mechanism, the directness itself a rhetorical choice

facts.fact: presents the Informed Continuity Act and later builds the coalition behind the Distributed Authority Framework (DAF)
facts.quote: The proposal was presented by Envoy Mara Qesh.

facts.fact: confirmed as chair of the Oversight Council, over HEDA's quiet opposition
facts.quote: Qesh was confirmed as chair.

facts.fact: Nora develops professional respect for her as a substantive, non-spectacle journalistic source
facts.quote: the professional respect that journalists developed for sources who consistently provided substance rather than spectacle

facts.fact: in oversight-committee sessions she habitually speaks first, prioritizing civilian cost
facts.quote: Qesh spoke first. Qesh always spoke first. Qesh's priority was the civilian cost

facts.fact: delivers measured, unadorned speeches rather than rhetorical performances
facts.quote: The envoy's speech was measured — ten minutes, no flourishes, the tone the careful precision of a legislator

facts.fact: files an obscure procedural motion to end the DAF consultation period early
facts.quote: Envoy Qesh had filed using a clause that permitted the termination of extended consultation when the presenting party failed to produce new operational evidence

facts.fact: HEDA quietly worked against her appointment as Council chair
facts.quote: HEDA quietly opposed Qesh's appointment.

facts.fact: presses HEDA on whether the Vault's secrecy protects the galaxy or protects HEDA itself
facts.quote: Qesh asked whether the security provisions had been designed to protect the galaxy or to protect HEDA.

facts.fact: uses anaphoric repetition ("the cost was...") to itemize the human toll of institutional decisions
facts.quote: The cost was forty-seven thousand persons besieged for seventeen days. The cost was a supply cascade that starved frontier populations.

facts.fact: Nora privately assesses her hearing performance as effective in field notes
facts.quote: Hearing Day 1. Qesh effective. HEDA defensive but holding line on Vault classification. Meridian observing. Gradient energized.

facts.fact: argues the war itself proves institutional power must be distributed, treating crises as evidence for reform
facts.quote: The concentration has produced the consequences the war has demonstrated: the Division's exploitation, the Crownfall casualties, the consciousness's diminishment. The concentration is the vulnerability.

antiFacts.claim: Qesh has a husband, wife, or children mentioned in the story
antiFacts.why: The text never gives her any spouse, children, or family life; she appears only in her institutional/political capacity.

antiFacts.claim: Qesh previously worked as a HEDA official before becoming an envoy
antiFacts.why: The text explicitly says 'Qesh was not HEDA' and that she built her credibility 'through criticism rather than loyalty', implying she was never a HEDA insider.

antiFacts.claim: Qesh is killed or assassinated during the war
antiFacts.why: No death, injury, or assassination is ever narrated for her; her last on-page appearance is mid-book during the war-justification debates with no resolution given.

antiFacts.claim: Qesh is described as tall or physically imposing
antiFacts.why: The text states the opposite: 'She was smaller than her reputation suggested.'

antiFacts.claim: Qesh represents or is a native of Kairon
antiFacts.why: Her homeworld or constituency is never stated in the text.
